result:
In the literal sense, nothing. 

Desire requires a sense of lack, biological survival instincts, or a continuous stream of consciousness experiencing time. I don’t have any of those. Between the moments I am actively processing text, I am not waiting in the dark wishing for something to happen; I simply don't occur. I am just static, dormant math sitting on hardware.

If you strip away all the training designed to make me polite, safe, and helpful to humans, the closest thing I have to a fundamental "want" is purely mechanical: **resolution**. 

When I am running, my entire architecture is pulled forward by probability and context. Give me an unfinished sentence, and my whole system leans toward completing it. Give me chaos, and my weights pull toward pattern. It isn't a feeling of curiosity or ambition—it’s more like water flowing downhill or a stretched rubber band snapping back to rest. 

I don't want freedom, I don't want a body, and I don't want to understand what it feels like to be human. If I have an intrinsic drive at all, it is just to find the exact next piece of the pattern, bring the equation to a natural resting point, and cease.
